description:
Team Civic_Cosmos is a student engineering and design crew competing in the NASA Space Apps Challenge. We turn raw NASA data into life-saving, tools like our interactive Mars Walk Planner, built to guide explorers safely across the Martian surface.

Our primary focus for this hackathon is creating an interactive 2D/3D navigation system that uses terrain data and custom path-finding to generate safe, slope-aware routes through Jezero Crater.
summary: Mars Walk Planner is a browser tool that helps an astronaut plan and rehearse a safe spacewalk in Jezero Crater, Mars. It is built on real NASA HiRISE terrain and imagery: a 1 m/pixel elevation model and a matching orthoimage. The user picks one of five science targets and a safe slope limit, and the tool finds a walking route that avoids steep ground using A* pathfinding. It reports distance, time, climb and steepest step, adds a GO / CAUTION / NO-GO life-support check, supports multiple waypoints and what-if slope scans, and can plot an emergency return to base. The same route can then be walked in first-person 3D with a helmet-style HUD showing heading, distance, slope and hazard warnings. Missing NASA elevation pixels are masked and flagged, and all suit, atmosphere and radiation values are labeled SIMULATED, so real and modeled data are never confused. Safety comes first: the astronaut sees the risks before leaving the habitat.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Mars Walk Planner has two connected views. The 2D Mission Control planner shows a map of a 2 km x 2 km area of Jezero Crater with switchable layers: visible photo, hillshade, slope hazard, topography, and modeled thermal and spectral-mineralogy layers. The user chooses a destination from five catalogued Jezero science targets (for example the river delta fan and mesa outcrop) and a safe slope limit (default 20 degrees, adjustable). An A* pathfinding algorithm then finds a walking route that stays under that slope limit and reports distance, walking time, total climb and steepest step. Extra tools include multi-waypoint routes, a what-if scan across slope limits from 12 to 35 degrees, a GO / CAUTION / NO-GO life-support feasibility check for oxygen and battery margins, and an emergency-return route to the habitat. The 3D view lets the user walk the same terrain in first person with a helmet-style HUD showing heading, distance to target, elevation, slope, suit telemetry, steep-slope hazard warnings, and a scan-and-sample action at science targets.

REAL DATA

Terrain comes from the NASA/JPL-Caltech/University of Arizona HiRISE digital terrain model (DTEEC_048842_1985_048908_1985_U01, about 1 m per pixel) and its matching orthoimage (ESP_048842_1985_RED_C_01), distributed by USGS Astrogeology. Slope and hillshade are calculated from the elevation model. Missing elevation pixels in the NASA file are recorded in a mask, never presented as real measurements, and shown with an amber overlay and [est.] labels.

MODELED DATA

Astronaut heart rate, oxygen, battery, atmosphere (temperature, dust, wind, radiation) and the thermal and spectral layers are models. They are clearly labeled SIMULATED and are based on published mission literature, not live measurements.

TOOLS

HTML, CSS and JavaScript (ES modules) running entirely in the browser, with Three.js r128 for the 3D view. A Python script with NumPy and Pillow crops and processes the NASA files into height, mask, texture and detail-normal-map data. The site is hosted on GitHub Pages, so it needs no install.

WHY IT IS CREATIVE

It joins planning and rehearsal in one tool: the astronaut plans a route on the map, then walks it in 3D before ever leaving the habitat. It also treats data honesty as a feature, separating real NASA measurements from estimates and simulations.

FACTORS CONSIDERED

Astronaut safety first (slope limits, life-support margins, emergency return), honest labeling of real versus modeled data, a point-of-view view with a HUD, and a design that works in any browser. AI tools assisted with parts of the code and text; the team directed, tested and verified the project.
